basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'VERS. 7.-- Dixitque Jacob pastoribus: Adhuc multum tempus diei superest. Quomodo Dominus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 7.-- Dixitque Jacob pastoribus: Adhuc multum tempus diei superest. Quomodo Dominus ista loquitur praedicatoribus, videlicet, quia multum spatium est amodo usque ad futuram resurrectionem, quod spatium diei non immerito comparatur; quia modo licet in claritate fidei consistentes bona usque ad finem saeculi operari. Nec tempus est ut ad caulas greges, id est ad mansiones coelestes, quia prius perfecte fideles instruendi sunt cognitione fidei. Unde et subditur: Date ante potum ovibus. Scilicet ac si dicatur: Instruite simpliciter simplices, | et sic ad pastum, hoc est ad meditationem Scripturarum, reducite.
